title: Turn your Apple Health workouts into a dashboard
summary: Phil Simon had Claude Code sort through his exported Apple Health data and build an interactive workout dashboard; he says it beats Apple Health and Strava, and shared it publicly.
agent_role: Claude Code wrote and ran the parsing script, produced statistics and built the dashboard; Simon posed the questions, such as how his HIIT calorie burn changed over the years.
what_they_did: Phil Simon wanted answers the free versions of Strava and Apple Health couldn't give. One example: how his Thursday high-intensity interval class calorie burn changed over the years. He exported his Apple Health data and had Claude write a small program to turn it into a clean spreadsheet file. He ran it in Claude Code for summary numbers. About forty more minutes produced an interactive dashboard, and he asked Claude everyday questions about his data.
how_it_went: He says the tool gives him far better insight into his exercise history than Apple Health or Strava. Instructor friends wanted to use it, so he shared it publicly on GitHub.
worth_knowing: The dashboard doesn't pick up new workouts on its own, so he must export and process the data again each time. Apple Health records no distance for strength and interval workouts, so treadmill miles from those classes are missing.
prompt: I've exported my Apple Health data to [path to export.xml]. Write a Python script that parses the workouts into a clean CSV with date, workout type, duration, calories and distance, run it, and show me summary stats by workout type and year. Point out any fields that are empty for certain workout types. Then build an interactive local dashboard that answers questions like: [your questions, e.g. average calories per [workout type] by year, workout time histogram, weekly patterns by day]. Show me the plan for the dashboard before building it.
